evidence: Linear LR schedule for IMP retraining, adaptive initial LR, budgeted dense training; claims outperforming unnamed state-of-the-art sparsification-during-training approaches; unspecified experiments.
rationale: Idiom paraphrased as a prescription to embrace retraining. Abstract says massively shortened and outperforms state-of-the-art, with no named benchmark or numbers: unspecified experiments.

evidence: Datatype-tagged prompts with GPT-2-small plus grammar decoder; GPT-4o-based primitives dataset, accuracy 0.58 to 0.82; counting and repeated-addition examples; single-GPU proof-of-concept.
rationale: Title 'boosting LLMs' and 'small models reliably emit code' generalise from one GPT-2-small model and one GPT-4o-generated dataset; 0.82 accuracy is not reliability.

evidence: Expressivity theory comparing soft prompting and prefix-tuning with full fine-tuning; argument that context-based tuning cannot change attention patterns; no experiments reported.
rationale: Question title answered with hedged theory ('potentially', 'may not'). Own claims stay within the theoretical argument, which is stated without experiments.

evidence: Qualitative and quantitative experiments on mini-batch SGD barrier crossing (unspecified); larger batches align with top Hessian eigenvectors; no named models or datasets.
rationale: Question title answered directly. 'Rarely crosses barriers during DNN optimization' and 'happens because' rest on unspecified experiments with no named models or measured mechanism.

evidence: ALIGN lightweight interface wrapper; experiments on embodied, web and tool-use domains; up to 45.67% success gain on ALFWorld; unnamed agent architectures and LLM backbones.
rationale: Generalising across unnamed architectures and backbones is H4 scope. 'Achieves the alignment' is definitive, but evidence shows success-rate gains, not measured alignment.

evidence: Pretraining 17 attention and gated-convolution LMs on the Pile (2.1 perplexity gap); recall analysis explaining 82% of gap; MQAR; hybrids closing 97.4% of gap.
rationale: 'Maintaining sub-quadratic scaling' is a design property asserted without any measurement (H1 pattern). Pile and recall results are named and quantified.

evidence: WorldSimBench dual evaluation: HF-Embodied human-feedback dataset and preference evaluator; action-level evaluation in three embodied scenarios; no models named.
rationale: 'Take the first step in evaluating' is an unhedged priority claim (H5). 'Aligns with human perception' is asserted with no agreement or validation reported.

evidence: Likelihood-free BO with LLM and chemistry-foundation priors, MCTS over tree partition, LLM clustering; unspecified experiments and ablations; no named benchmarks.
rationale: 'Substantially improves' scalability, robustness and sample efficiency rests on unspecified experiments, with no benchmark, baseline or number given.

evidence: Explicit (2N+4)L-layer transformer simulating L gradient steps of N-layer ReLU network; approximation and convergence guarantees; softmax extension; synthetic validation at 3, 4, 6 layers.
rationale: 'Deep model training' is a class, but evidence covers ReLU networks on synthetic data (class generalisation). 'A deep neural network' and 'more practical setting' follow the same pattern.

evidence: Initial study: transfer quality under supervised and unsupervised task sequences, no degradation with full fine-tuning; GLAD proposed, no reported results; no datasets named.
rationale: Title says the pretrainer increments generalisation, but only a no-degradation finding and design-based GLAD are reported. 'Novel problem' is an H5 claim; 'efficient' is unmeasured.

evidence: VFedCD shallow-encoder/deep-decoder framework with CTV and SDP; unspecified experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets; accuracy vs centralized methods; privacy from design.
rationale: 'The first framework for causal discovery in vertical federated settings' is an unhedged priority claim (H5). 'Guaranteeing privacy' is asserted from design with no privacy evaluation (H1).

evidence: Attention replaced by convolutions with comparable performance; MetaFormer principle; Fourier global-aware convolution streaming; consistent gains on deblurring, denoising, deraining.
rationale: 'Architecture matters' is backed by the convolution-replacement result. The module is said to enhance long-range dependency capture, a design benefit with no measurement (H1).

evidence: RAVEn pretraining on LRS3; low- and high-resource VSR and ASR results; surpasses self-supervised VSR methods; 30 h self-training beats a 90,000 h semi-supervised method.
rationale: 'Powerful speech representations entirely from raw video and audio' generalises from LRS3 results on two tasks (H2). SOTA claims name LRS3 and are not overreach.

evidence: Human step-by-step demonstration dataset in a crafting grid world; language-conditioned hierarchical policy; zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks; few-demo learning.
rationale: Title prescribes a practice for reinforcement learning in general, but evidence covers one grid-world environment (class generalisation). 'Gives interpretable behaviors' follows from the design, unmeasured.

evidence: Single-scene multi-scale generative radiance volume; demonstrations of plausible diverse variations; unnamed comparisons with state-of-the-art generative scene methods; editing, composition and animation uses.
rationale: 'A 3D generative model for general natural scenes' rests on unspecified scenes. The claimed merits over state-of-the-art methods have no named baseline or metric.

evidence: ELMo-style embeddings from a program corpus, fine-tuned for bug detection; claimed improvement of an unnamed state-of-the-art bug detector; no dataset named.
rationale: Claims to improve a state-of-the-art bug detector, but the system, dataset and metric are unnamed, so the SOTA claim rests on unspecified experiments.

evidence: Diffusion-bridge Hi-C resolution enhancement with diffusion augmentation; comparison to existing models on standard vision metrics; downstream structure and loop analyses; human cells.
rationale: Claims are tied to the reported comparisons and downstream analyses. 'Surpasses existing models' is a direct comparison, not a best or state-of-the-art claim.

evidence: Memorization-vs-generalization estimator; capacity about 3.6 bits per parameter across hundreds of transformer LMs (500K to 1.5B); grokking observation; scaling laws.
rationale: Question title answered by a capacity estimate across a range of transformer sizes. 'Modern language models' reaches beyond the sizes trained: a generality flag, not overreach here.

evidence: Backtracking via [RESET] token with SFT or DPO; Llama-3-8B unsafe rate 6.1% to 1.5%; no helpfulness regression; four adversarial attacks including an adaptive one.
rationale: Title's 'generation safety' is general, but evidence is one model, Llama-3-8B. 'Models trained to backtrack are consistently safer' generalises from that single model (H2).

evidence: GEP projects gradients onto an anchor subspace and perturbs embedding and residual separately; epsilon=8 accuracy 74.9% CIFAR10, 95.1% SVHN; unnamed existing results.
rationale: 'Low computational cost' is asserted with no cost measure (H1). 'Greatly helps to break the dimensional barrier' is a mechanism claim with no dimension analysis reported.

evidence: QuArch benchmark: 2,671 expert-validated QA pairs on processor design, memory and interconnects; frontier accuracies 34% to 72%; analysis, design, implementation categories.
rationale: 'The first benchmark designed to' is an unhedged priority claim with no evidence of priority (H5). Accuracy range and category results are named and quantified.

evidence: Hybrid online/offline RL sample augmentation for IL branching; unspecified evaluations on many MIP problems vs learning-based models, SCIP and Gurobi; no benchmark named.
rationale: 'Superior to state-of-the-art' and 'often outperforms Gurobi' rest on unnamed MIP problems. 'Reduces training complexity' follows from design and is not measured (H1).

evidence: SimPLe video-prediction model-based RL on Atari with 100k interactions; architecture comparison incl. a novel best one; beats model-free methods in most games, 10x+ in some.
rationale: Best-in-setting and outperforming state-of-the-art claims are on named Atari games under a stated 100k-interaction regime, so they stay within the evidence.

evidence: Adaptive label smoothing from relative object size; ImageNet overconfidence results; order-of-magnitude confidence drop on context-only images vs baselines; +0.021 AP on MS COCO.
rationale: 'One size doesn't fit all' is a negated universal supported by adaptive-versus-fixed gains. 'CNNs trained using adaptive label smoothing are much less likely' generalises from ImageNet alone (H2).

evidence: Constrained universal approximation theorem for non-convex compact sets via probabilistic transformers; deep Berge theorem with soft constraints; exact convex-constraint classical result.
rationale: Title drops the convex-constraint and probabilistic-transformer conditions the abstract states. 'First universal approximation theorem for classical transformers' is a priority claim (H5).

evidence: wav2tok CTC/EM-learned discrete tokens from similar audio pairs; experiments on music search (query by humming) and speech search; claimed outperformance of unnamed state-of-the-art baselines.
rationale: 'Learns representations for any kind of audio' generalises from music and speech retrieval. 'Efficient retrieval' and 'faster to match' are design-based speed claims, untimed (H1).

evidence: Theoretical bounds on classifier susceptibility to adversarial examples for certain problem classes; experiments on real-world problems exploring dimensionality and image complexity.
rationale: Question title is answered for 'certain classes of problems', as the abstract restricts it. Bounds and experiments support the stated claims.

evidence: LayoutDETR detection-based layout generation; new state of the art on unnamed public benchmarks and own ad-banner dataset; user study preferring it to baselines.
rationale: Title generalises 'Detection Transformer' from one DETR-based method. 'New state of the art' on unnamed benchmarks and 'significant margins' without numbers rest on unspecified comparisons.

evidence: High-norm artifact tokens identified in supervised and self-supervised ViTs; extra register tokens; state of the art on unnamed dense prediction tasks; smoother feature and attention maps.
rationale: 'Need registers' asserts necessity but shows a sufficient fix (H7). 'Fixes that problem entirely' and state of the art on unnamed dense tasks exceed the reported evidence.

evidence: Theoretical framework on when weak supervision guarantees disentanglement under distribution matching; empirical checks of restricted labeling, match-pairing, rank-pairing.
rationale: 'With guarantees' is unconditional in the title, but the abstract makes guarantees depend on the weak-supervision method and distribution matching, and notes they may be absent.

evidence: BRAC+ with analytical KL bound, state-dependent Lagrange multipliers and OOD gradient penalty; unnamed challenging offline RL benchmarks; claimed outperformance of state-of-the-art methods.
rationale: 'Outperforms the state-of-the-art' is asserted on unnamed benchmarks. 'Reduce variance' and 'Q values are bounded' follow from design and are not measured (H1).

evidence: Extensive experiments on learning-rate rewinding and 1-cycle schedules; large learning rate claimed as cause; random pruning with large-LR retraining matches or beats methodical pruning.
rationale: 'The reason behind the success is the large learning rate' is a single-cause claim resting on unspecified experiments. The title is supported by the named schedules.

evidence: None reported. Abstract describes an analytic policy gradient through an embedded model, with Q and V learned from real or imaginary data.
rationale: No experiments reported. 'Can reduce the variance of the gradient estimation' follows from the design and is not measured, the H1 example pattern.

evidence: Procedural generator of DAG-structured 2D adventure puzzles with ground-truth solutions; exponentially scaling layouts; experiments on current multimodal LLM/VLM agents.
rationale: Benchmark claims stay within the generator and reported agent experiments. 'Rigorous testbed for general-purpose embodied reasoning' is an aspiration, not a result.

evidence: Robust versus non-robust feature learning dynamics; two pathways depending on hyperparameters; strong unspecified empirical evidence; theory in a simplified setting; hedged cross-dataset observation.
rationale: Title says SGD learns robust features first without condition, but the abstract shows two hyperparameter-dependent pathways (H6). 'Neural networks' is a class supported by unspecified experiments.

evidence: Structure-aware vocabulary from Foldseek structure tokens; SaProt trained on about 40M sequences and structures; surpasses unnamed baselines across 10 unnamed downstream tasks.
rationale: 'General-purpose' and 'broad applicability' rest on ten downstream tasks the abstract does not name (H4). Baselines are unnamed, so the comparison cannot be checked here.

evidence: BERT-fused NMT: BERT representations fused into encoder and decoder layers; supervised, semi-supervised and unsupervised MT; state of the art on seven benchmark datasets, none named.
rationale: State of the art on seven unnamed benchmark datasets rests on unspecified experiments. 'Preliminary exploration' is a hedge on the motivating step, not overreach.

evidence: Word-scrambling transfer tests: LSTM with GloVe, BERT and baselines on four classification and two sequence labeling tasks; analyses of pretraining, fine-tuning, word frequency.
rationale: Claims are scoped to named models and task types, with hedged framing. 'Can guide future studies' is an impact statement, not a result, so it is not scored.

evidence: SLAC latent variable model with latent critic on image observations; compared with VAE representations, model-free and model-based RL on difficult control tasks.
rationale: 'Much more efficiently than standard RL methods' is an unquantified magnitude on unnamed control tasks. 'Substantially' over the named VAE baseline is not overreach.

evidence: Markovian compressors in QSGD with momentum; convergence proofs for non-convex, PL and strongly convex cases; momentum variant proven faster; practical wins over unnamed algorithms.
rationale: Title credits Markovian compression with acceleration, but the proven speedup is for the momentum variant and practical gains are not isolated (H1). 'Should accelerate' is intuition.

evidence: Empirical study of STE-trained binary weight networks: scaling-factor changes add little, sign changes crucial; sign-fixed primary subnetworks; QBN kernel method, no results reported.
rationale: 'Breaks the common wisdom' and compressibility are hedged hypotheses, and the QBN method has no reported results (H1 pattern). Sign-stability findings are supported.

evidence: End-to-end adaptive-kernel SVM with Siamese kernel; one-shot audio redefinition; Omniglot 98.1% to 98.5% (one-shot), 98.9% to 99.3% (few-shot); TIMIT tested, no results.
rationale: 'Make SVM great again' rests on small gains on one vision dataset. 'Eliminates the problem of choosing a correct kernel' claims elimination where only improvement is shown (H3).

evidence: FIM principal-eigenvalue robustness metric; closed-form spectral bounds for ReLU and convolution; theory comparing VGG, ResNet, DenseNet, Transformer; unspecified experiments.
rationale: 'To enable scalable computation' asserts an efficiency benefit from algorithm choice with no scaling measurement (H1). The theory, bounds and named architectures are supported.

evidence: Mechanistic analysis of trained Gemma 7B: highest RoPE frequencies used for positional attention, lowest for likely semantics; proofs; experiments on a RoPE modification.
rationale: Question answered with hedged single-model analysis ('unlikely', 'we suspect'). 'Greatly prefers' and 'in general' rest on one model, but claims are kept to Gemma 7B.

evidence: UNITER pretraining on COCO, VG, Conceptual Captions, SBU with MLM, ITM, MRM; conditioned vs unconditioned masking; pretraining-task ablation; SOTA on six named V+L tasks.
rationale: SOTA and ablation claims name their tasks and pretraining datasets, and stay within the evaluated tasks. No overreach found.

evidence: Clustering annotators from anonymously annotated data; L2D-Clusters defers to clusters; clusters align with annotator behaviour; comparable to expert L2D, esp. onboarding.
rationale: Comparability and the onboarding benefit are direction-only results on unnamed data. The abstract makes no magnitude, state-of-the-art or breadth claim.

evidence: Iterative MCMC-inspired sampling from base-model likelihoods, no training; comparable or better than RL on MATH500, HumanEval, GPQA across base models; diversity claim without numbers.
rationale: 'Broad applicability beyond easily verifiable domains' is untested (H4). The claim that the sampler avoids diversity collapse has no supporting evidence in the abstract.

evidence: PerContrast causal-intervention personal-token identification (87.8% F1 on own benchmark); EM-based PerCE loss; several LLMs; LongLaMP gains averaging over 10% and up to 40.57%.
rationale: 'Strong cross-task and cross-scenario transferability' names no tasks or scenarios (H4). 'Minimal additional cost' is asserted without any measured cost (H1).

evidence: Closed-form large-qubit generalization analysis vs quantum kernel bandwidth; generalization for well-aligned targets; empirical checks on unnamed challenging datasets, some outside assumptions.
rationale: 'Bandwidth enables generalization' omits the well-aligned-target condition the abstract states (H6). Success 'far outside our theoretical assumptions' names no dataset.

evidence: Context reliance tracked during instruction finetuning on TULU, Alpaca, Ultrachat for Llama, Mistral, Pythia; controlled data studies; theory; mitigations with limited gains.
rationale: Hedged title ('may not') is supported by a phenomenon observed across three datasets and three model families. Controlled studies and theory back its explanation.
